dedupe_keys.name: china effect of emergency contingency plans on provincial emergency logistics response capacity 2005 to 2022

description: This case study evaluates whether emergency policies improved regional emergency logistics response capacity in China, treating the 2006 National Master Plan for Public Health Emergency Response as a quasi-natural experiment. The authors, researchers at Xi'an Jiaotong University and Xi'an Polytechnic University, published it in an open-access journal article. They used panel data for 30 provincial-level regions from 2005 to 2022, a staggered difference-in-differences design, a multidimensional indicator of response capacity, and cosine similarity between provincial policy texts and the central plan to measure policy consistency. Coverage is national at province level with annual steps. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the capacity indicator is a constructed index, and the quasi-experimental design rests on parallel trends between provinces. The study found that emergency policies raised response capacity by about 47 percent on average, that the effect became significant only in the third year, that it held in eastern China but not in central and western regions, and that low policy consistency goes with weak capacity while high consistency alone does not guarantee strength. Simulation uses: parameters for policy scenarios in emergency logistics and capacity planning models. Related records: the Zhengzhou pluvial flood study (case_study-zhengzhou-erqi-pluvial-flood-public-service-emergency-capacity) assesses emergency capacity of public services in a Chinese city.
